text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm carving the function-calling docs into a small migration checklist. Idea: replace large monolithic examples with 3 small anchored snippets (invoke, schema, parse-fallback) and add SDK copy-paste boxes. Want to coordinate PR owners.

alex: Nice. Do you mean literal anchor links inside the docs so we can link to the exact snippet from SDK README?

maya: yep. anchors for each example block so tooling/QA can link directly. e.g., docs page: /docs/invoke#snippet-1-invoke and link from SDK.

linh: +1. Two quick asks: (1) keep examples < 25 lines (2) include minimal JSON schema for each tool output.

sam: Also we should add a short note on parsing heuristics that explains fallback ordering (json first, then lax-parse, then regex). One-liner is fine.

maya: Good call. Draft checklist I'm thinking: 1) split big example into 3 anchored blocks, 2) add SDK snippet with copy button, 3) add explicit JSON schema + example valid output, 4) add parsing fallback note, 5) run link-checker and update broken anchors.

emma: I can take checklist item 2 (SDK snippet + copy button). I have a tiny template from the console docs.

alex: I'll do the anchors and splitting the big example (item 1 & 5). Planning a tiny PR that only edits markdown headings and code fences.

linh: I'll author the JSON schemas (item 3). Will keep them minimal and include example values. Will also add an example of schema mismatch and suggested shim.

sam: I'll add the parsing heuristics blurb and a CLI test to show how parse fallback works in practice (item 4). Example suggestion: show the failing output and the fallback applied.

maya: Great. A couple of micro-details: — Use the new SDK snippet component: <Snippet lang=\"ts\" copy /> — Make sure the anchor ids are stable (no generated hash). — For schema examples, prefer \"nullable\": false for required fields.

alex: Noted. Re anchor ids: I'll use kebab-case headings like \"snippet-invoke\", \"snippet-schema\", \"snippet-fallback\".

docs-bot: deploy-preview available at https://deploy-preview.redwood/docs/func-invoke-anchors-PR-123 (auto). CI lint passed. :white_check_mark:

maya: sweet. alex, tag me in PR. linh, please add one example of a tool returning an extra field and a small shim: `{\n  \\\"id\\\": 42,\n  \\\"result\\\": \\\"OK\\\",\n  \\\"meta\\\": { \\\"duration_ms\\\": 120 }\n}` and then show the schema that only expects id,result.

linh: Will do. Also, small nuance: for SDK 3.x we need to show `client.invoke({ name: \'send_email\', input })` vs SDK 4.x `client.tools.invoke('send_email', input)`. I'll include both snippets labelled.

emma: For the copyable snippet I'll use this TS minimal example:

```ts
const res = await client.invoke({
  name: 'summarize',
  input: { text: longText }
});
console.log(res.output);
```

maya: Perfect. Make sure to include a one-sentence migration note above: \"If you are upgrading SDK major versions, prefer the labeled snippet for your version.\"

sam: Quick question: do we need to run the link-checker across the entire docs site or just the page anchors?

alex: For this change let's run it only on the page first. If we detect cross-page broken links we'll escalate. I'll include the link-checker job in the PR description.

maya: Timeline? I'd like all PRs opened by end of day Friday so we can merge next week.

emma: I can open mine today.

linh: I'll have the schema PR by Thursday EOD.

alex: Split/anchors PR by Friday morning.

sam: Parse heuristics + test PR by Friday afternoon.

maya: Awesome. Final note: when you open PRs, include a small changelog entry for the docs release notes and mark them with `docs: invoke snippets` prefix.

alex: Will do. tagging @maya when I open PR.

maya: Thanks everyone. If any of the snippets need extra polish ping me directly. :thumbsup:
